title: Make `st.multiselect` not wrap the selected options / keep its height
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests. - [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue. ### Summary If you select many options in `st.multiselect`, they wrap to multiple lines. This makes the widget grow in height and can make layouts look bad: In some situations, it would be nice to make the options not wrap but e.g. require the user to scroll to see them: ### Why? The current style is annoying in some situations: 1. In compact layouts, this can use up a lot of space. 2. When placing the multiselect side by side with another widget like `st.selectbox` or `st.button`, it can look awkward if they have different height. ### How? I think there are situation where you want the options to wrap but others where you don't want that. So probably needs a parameter, e.g. `wrap=False|True`. And/or we could show the selected options in the dropdown, even though that would probably require us to move to a different component. ### Additional Context Related: - #12583 - #12582 - #5003 - #6592 - #13516

This is a **feature request / enhancement** for `st.multiselect`. When many options are selected, the chips wrap onto multiple lines, causing the widget to grow vertically and break compact layouts or misalign with adjacent widgets (e.g. `st.selectbox`, `st.button`). The request is to add a way to keep the widget's height fixed, e.g. a `wrap=False` parameter that keeps selected chips on a single (scrollable) line, and/or to summarize selections in the dropdown. Since this is a widget-styling/layout behavior with a small, well-scoped surface, the existing `type:enhancement`, `feature:st.multiselect`, `area:layout`, and `papercut` labels fit well. This is part of a broader family of "control wrap behavior" requests the author has filed across widgets and containers.

### Related Issues

- [#13516 — Option to not wrap `st.segmented_control` while displaying on a page](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13516): The closest analog — another chip/tag-based widget where the request is an option to prevent items from wrapping. A shared solution/API (`wrap=False`) would likely apply to both.
- [#12582 — Control wrap behavior for horizontal `st.container`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12582): Same `wrap=False` concept applied to horizontal containers; part of the same wrap-control theme and directly cross-referenced in this issue.
- [#12583 — Control wrap behavior for text (`st.markdown`, `st.text`, ...)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12583): Requests a `wrap=False` parameter to avoid text wrapping (truncating instead); same underlying layout-control motivation and also cross-referenced here.

## Update

Streamlit 1.62+ will provide a `wrap` parameter that allows to keep the mutliselect at a single row height via wrap=False.
